newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba's tourism arrivals, income grow in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Cuba's tourism arrivals, income grow in 1996.

text.p: Cuba's tourism industry, the fastest-growing economic sector on the communist-ruled island, will end 1996 with gross earnings of more than $1.3 billion and record arrivals of close to a million foreign visitors, state media reported on Sunday.
Figures provided by the Tourism Ministry showed that up to Dec. 26, some 966,267 tourists had visited the Caribbean island. This compared with 740,000 who travelled to Cuba in 1995.
Tourism officials expected to finish the year with close to one million arrivals. Most visitors to Cuba came from Italy, followed by Canada, Spain, Germany, France and other nations.
The 1996 gross revenues from tourism, which included related activities like tourism flights, represented an increase of more than $200 million over the previous year's earnings of $1.1 billion.
Tourism has overtaken sugar as the island's biggest hard currency earner in gross income terms.
Cuba's tourism industry raised accomodation capacity to 27,000 rooms in 1996, adding 4,200 rooms during the year through construction of new hotels and refurbishment of others.

Cuba's tourist sector has also proved one of the most attractive to foreign investment. Spanish, Canadian, German, French, Italian and Mexican companies are among those who operate either joint ventures, management contracts or other tourism projects on the island.
But the sector is not without its problems. A senior Cuban official said earlier this month that delays in completing new hotels in Cuba had cost the island some $41 million in lost tourism revenue.
